title: Rotate Image
statement:
You're given an n x n grid of integers, `matrix`, that represents an image. Rotate the image 90 degrees clockwise.

Do it in place: change `matrix` itself rather than building a second grid and returning it. Your function returns nothing; after it runs, `matrix` should hold the rotated image.

Constraints: 1 <= n <= 20; -1000 <= matrix[i][j] <= 1000.

examples.explanation: The left column, read bottom to top, becomes the top row.
The output shows matrix after your function has run.
A 1 x 1 image looks the same after rotating.

hints: Pick one cell, say row 0 column 1 in a 3 x 3 grid. Where does it end up after a clockwise turn?
Writing the rotated values into a new grid is easy. What stops you from simply overwriting cells in place?
Can you get the same result from two simpler moves that each swap values in place?
Try flipping the grid across its main diagonal and look at what's left to do. Watch out for swapping each pair twice.
Transpose (swap matrix[i][j] with matrix[j][i] for j > i), then reverse every row.
followUps: What are the time and space complexity, and why can't the time be better than O(n^2)?
How would you rotate counter-clockwise instead, using the same building blocks?
Can you do it in one pass by moving four cells at a time in a cycle, and what are the loop bounds?
What changes if the grid is m x n rather than square, and can it still be done in place?
idealAnswerPoints: Works out where cell (i, j) lands: it moves to (j, n - 1 - i)
Rotates in place, either transpose then reverse each row, or four-way swaps layer by layer
Only swaps above the diagonal when transposing so pairs aren't swapped back
States O(n^2) time and O(1) extra space
weakAnswerSigns: Builds a new grid and returns it, leaving matrix unchanged
Rebinds the local name with matrix = ..., which the caller never sees
Transposes the whole grid and swaps every pair twice
Mixes up clockwise and counter-clockwise and can't check it on a 2 x 2 example

rubric.correctness: matrix holds the clockwise rotation after the call for every size from 1 x 1 up, including negatives and repeated values.
rubric.efficiency: O(n^2) time and O(1) extra space; an extra grid counts against efficiency unless the candidate names it.
rubric.code_quality: Two clear in-place steps or a well-bounded four-way swap, no off-by-one in the loop limits.
rubric.communication: Derives the index mapping before coding and checks it on a small grid.
